section: Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
label: Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: The Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws.
chapter: Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

label: v1 · Chapter XV The Discovery of Oz, the Terrible
value: Oz is revealed to be a ventriloquist from Omaha.
chapter: v1 · Chapter XV The Discovery of Oz, the Terrible
unit: The group returns to the Emerald City and eventually gains an audience with the Great Oz after threatening to call the Winged Monkeys. When Toto knocks over a screen in the Throne Room, Oz is revealed to be an ordinary old man and ventriloquist from Omaha who has been fooling everyone. Despite admitting he is a humbug without real magic, he promises to grant the group their requests the following day.

label: Scarecrow
value: The Scarecrow uses his intellect to protect the Lion.
unit: The Cowardly Lion initial encounter with the Scarecrow involves an attack, but they quickly become loyal traveling companions after the Lion reveals his secret cowardice. The Lion uses his immense physical strength to help the group cross obstacles, while the Scarecrow uses his intellect to protect the Lion, including devising a rescue plan with field mice when the Lion falls asleep in a field of poisonous poppies. Their mutual reliance and concern for each other's safety solidify a close friendship during their journey.

label: Appearance
value: The Wicked Witch possesses only a single eye.
unit: The Wicked Witch possesses only a single eye. Despite having just one eye, it is remarkably powerful, functioning like a telescope that allows her to see everywhere and look out across great distances.

passages.v01:c14:p0010: Now the Wicked Witch of the West had but one eye, yet that was as powerful as a telescope, and could see everywhere. So, as she sat in the door of her castle, she happened to look around and saw Dorothy lying asleep, with her friends all about her. They were a long distance off, but the Wicked Witch was angry to find them in her country; so she blew upon a silver whistle that hung around her neck.
passages.v01:c14:p0021: Now this same morning the Wicked Witch came to the door of her castle and looked out with her one eye that could see far off. label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: A deep ditch blocks the yellow brick road.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

label: v1 · Chapter X The Guardian of the Gate
value: The Guardian leads the group inside the Emerald City.
chapter: v1 · Chapter X The Guardian of the Gate
unit: The Cowardly Lion awakens and rejoins Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and Toto as they journey along the yellow brick road toward the Emerald City. They spend the night at a farm house, where a local man tells them about the mysterious Great Oz and his ability to grant their wishes. The next day, the group reaches the gates of the Emerald City, where the Guardian locks green-tinted spectacles onto each of them before leading them inside.

value: The Stork rescues the Scarecrow.

value: Dorothy's house inadvertently crushes the Wicked Witch of the East

unit: Dorothy wakes up to find her house has landed safely in a beautiful land, inadvertently crushing the Wicked Witch of the East. To return home, the Witch of the North advises Dorothy to travel along the yellow brick road to the Emerald City to seek help from the Great Wizard Oz, blessing her with a protective kiss before departing.

label: v1 · Chapter XXI The Lion Becomes the King of Beasts
value: The travelers enter a grand forest.

unit: The travelers trek through a swampy region into a grand forest, which the Lion finds delightful. They come across a gathering of forest animals terrorized by a giant, spider-like monster. The Lion offers to kill the beast in exchange for becoming their King, tracks down the sleeping creature, and decapitates it with a single blow. The animals joyfully pledge their allegiance to him as King of the Forest.

label: Personality
value: The Wizard is reputed to be capable of shapeshifting into any form.
unit: Though reputed to be a good and wise entity capable of shapeshifting into any form, the Wizard admits that while he is a good man, he is actually a very bad Wizard. He is motivated by a desire to return to Kansas and work in a circus once again.

passages.v01:c04:p0050: “He is a good Wizard. Whether he is a man or not I cannot tell, for I have never seen him.”
passages.v01:c12:p0025: “That is hard to tell,” said the man thoughtfully. “You see, Oz is a Great Wizard, and can take on any form he wishes. So that some say he looks like a bird; and some say he looks like an elephant; and some say he looks like a cat. To others he appears as a beautiful fairy, or a brownie, or in any other form that pleases him. But who the real Oz is, when he is in his own form, no living person can tell.”
passages.v01:c12:p0049: “It has been many years since anyone asked me to see Oz,” he said, shaking his head in perplexity. “He is powerful and terrible, and if you come on an idle or foolish errand to bother the wise reflections of the Great Wizard, he might be angry and destroy you all in an instant.”
passages.v01:c12:p0050: “But it is not a foolish errand, nor an idle one,” replied the Scarecrow; “it is important. And we have been told that Oz is a good Wizard.”
passages.v01:c17:p0074: “Oh, no, my dear; I’m really a very good man, but I’m a very bad Wizard, I must admit.”
passages.v01:c19:p0013: “Yes, of course,” replied Oz. “I am tired of being such a humbug. If I should go out of this Palace my people would soon discover I am not a Wizard, and then they would be vexed with me for having deceived them. So I have to stay shut up in these rooms all day, and it gets tiresome. I’d much rather go back to Kansas with you and be in a circus again.”

screen.reason: Passages indicate that the Wizard can take on any form he wishes, as stated by characters in the text.

value: Gayelette is capable of using her abilities to mold someone into being good.
unit: Gayelette is a character who possesses powerful magic. She is capable of using her abilities to mold someone into being strong, good, and lovely.

passages.v01:c16:p0033: “There lived here then, away at the North, a beautiful princess, who was also a powerful sorceress. All her magic was used to help the people, and she was never known to hurt anyone who was good. Her name was Gayelette, and she lived in a handsome palace built from great blocks of ruby. Everyone loved her, but her greatest sorrow was that she could find no one to love in return, since all the men were much too stupid and ugly to mate with one so beautiful and wise. At last, however, she found a boy who was handsome and manly and wise beyond his years. Gayelette made up her mind that when he grew to be a man she would make him her husband, so she took him to her ruby palace and used all her magic powers to make him as strong and good and lovely as any woman could wish. When he grew to manhood, Quelala, as he was called, was said to be the best and wisest man in all the land, while his manly beauty was so great that Gayelette loved him dearly, and hastened to make everything ready for the wedding.

screen.reason: The passage states that Gayelette used her magic powers to make Quelala as strong and good and lovely as any woman could wish.

value: They construct the balloon together.

unit: Oz summons Dorothy and proposes building a hot-air balloon so they can both cross the desert and return home. They construct the balloon together, but as it inflates and prepares to depart before a gathered crowd, Toto runs off. By the time Dorothy retrieves Toto, the ropes snap, and the balloon floats away with Oz alone, leaving Dorothy behind.

label: Cowardly Lion
value: After overcoming many perils together, they shared a joyous reunion.
unit: Dorothy first met the Cowardly Lion when he ambushed her friends in a forest; after he threatened Toto, Dorothy slapped his nose and scolded his cowardice, leading him to join her journey to ask Oz for courage. After overcoming many perils together, they shared a joyous reunion and continued traveling together until Dorothy found her way home.
